configs.description: The TM-8001 as ordered with two AC supplies, SFP+ cages unpopulated.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: telco.com publishes data sheets only; hardware documentation is on a support portal behind a login, whose contact is on telco.com/support. Searched: the telco.com media library, every product and knowledge-centre page, and the Wayback index of telco.com PDFs.
gaps.wanted: the TM-8001 / T-Metro 8001 hardware installation guide, from the BATM support portal.

gaps.note: Every vendor image is a three-quarter render; the face is measured through a homography of the best one, which is exact for the flat face and approximate for anything that stands proud of it.
gaps.wanted: a square-on photograph of the front at 4 px/mm or better.

gaps.note: The two hot-swappable supplies (AC PSU or -48 VDC PEM) are not on the front and nothing held shows the rear, so they are not modelled and the device has no supply bays.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear, or the installation guide's rear view.

gaps.note: The render shows the fan tray's wheel, its FAN TRAY legend and a small screw, but no seam, so the tray's extent on the face is unknown and it is not modelled as a bay.
gaps.wanted: a square-on or close photograph of the right end of the front.

gaps.note: No edition states the MNG port's rate; the data sheets list only "Console" among the management interfaces. 1g is carried as a BORROWED value from the TM-8104 (see provenance.mng-speed), not as a finding.

gaps.wanted: which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold
`cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on port group sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: 1RU x 440 x 44 x 508 deep. Depth, weight and 1RU are the data sheets' ("1.75'H (1RU) x 19'W x 20'D (44.45 x 482.6 x 508 mm)"; 482.6 is the 19-inch face with ears). WIDTH AND HEIGHT ARE BOTH ASSUMED, NOT MEASURED. A homography fixes the face's proportions only up to the rectangle it is mapped onto, and the 440 x 44 target was chosen: at 440 the in-block SFP+ pitch reads 14.24 +/- 0.22 mm, which agrees with the registry's ganged 14.25 - but that agreement is the ASSUMPTION restated, not a check. This vendor's own pitch, read off the TM810x stencil on the TM-8104, is 14.355, which would put the body at about 443.6. 44.0 is 1RU less the usual clearance. Every x on this face scales with the width, so all of them share this uncertainty (about 0.8%).

fan-tray.note: Data sheets: "Redundant hot-swappable ... fan tray" and "Fan: Load sharing, speed controlled, hot-swappable". The render prints FAN TRAY between two hazard triangles beside a large knurled wheel at the right, with a small screw left of it, so the tray is serviced from the front. ITS OUTLINE IS NOT VISIBLE - no seam shows in the render - so it is not drawn as a bay; the wheel is drawn as a fastener (see the fan-tray gap).

front-layout.note: Every feature is read off the 2025 render (telco.com 2025/08/8001@2x.png, 1678 px) after a four-corner homography of its front face onto a 440 x 44 rectangle at 10 px/mm - a planar face under perspective is exactly what a homography undoes, so this is a measurement, not a reading of a slanted picture. Corners in the render: TL (90, 309), TR (1361, 376), BR (1366, 512), BL (91, 434), each good to a pixel, which is about 0.35 mm across and 0.35 mm down. Features that stand proud of the face (the fan-tray wheel, the screws) are displaced by their own height and are estimated.

lamps.note: The per-port lamps are NOT under their ports: twenty dots in five colour strips, four to a strip, running x 157-287 under blocks 2-4, each strip the colour of its block and numbered with its first port (1, 5, 9, 13, 17). Dot centres measured, 1.6-2.0 mm, drawn as common/led-dot@1. FAN (red), PWR A and PWR B are round lamps in a column at x 55.5; FLT and STS are small lamps under blocks 1 and 2. FAN, PWR A and PWR B sit behind large domed lenses, about 7.6 mm across in the rectified render (FAN's red), drawn as bezels behind the 4 mm lamp part. No document says what any state means. A small printed "+" at about (297, 36), under block 4, is not identified by anything held and is not drawn.

mgmt-plates.note: CLI and MNG each sit on a raised plate held by a screw above and below the jack (x 3.5-25.3 and 27-48.8). Whether these are removable modules is not documented; they are drawn as panel plates with their screws.

mng-speed.note: BORROWED, NOT STATED. No TM-8001 edition gives the MNG port's rate (all three searched for 10/100, 1000, RJ-45, out-of-band and management port). 1g is taken from the TM-8104's OOB port, same vendor, same BiNOX OS generation and the same CLI / OOB pair, which NetBox's community entry types 1000base-t - itself unsourced. It is carried so the DCIM export does not guess, and the mng-speed gap stays open until a document states the real rate.

model.note: TM-8001 data sheet (telco.com 2025/12), "TM-8001 Compact 10GE Service Demarcation Device"; the 2019 and 2025-09 editions call it the T-Metro 8001, which the face prints.

ports.note: Twenty cage openings segmented in the rectified render, mean 13.4 x 8.7 at y 23.35, in blocks starting at x 71.6, 133.4, 193.8, 254.2 and 313.8. The raw centres scatter about 0.2 mm, which at a 14.24 mean pitch would overlap neighbouring cages, so each block is drawn REGULAR - four std/sfp-ganged@1 at the registry's 14.25 pitch, centred on the block's measured mean centre. BOTH JACKS ARE common/rj45-eth@1, turned 180: the render shows lamp windows along the top edge of both openings, CLI's as well as MNG's, so the lamped keyway side is up on each. That puts the CLI console on a lamped part, which L76 reports; it is left in the baseline, as on the TM-8104, whose console jack shows the same windows. Numbered 1-20 left to right in white on each block's colour bar (green 1-4, orange 5-8, blue 9-12, cyan 13-16, pink 17-20).

power.note: "Max power consumption: 150W" in all three editions, unqualified. Supplies: "Dual redundant, hot-swappable AC/DC 100-240VAC / -48VDC (-36VDC to -60VDC)", ordered as TM8001-AC-x (2 x AC PSU) or TM8001-DC (2 x -48 VDC PEM). They are not on the front, so they are presumably at the rear, which nothing shows.

sources.note: Three data-sheet editions (2019-01, 2025-09, 2025-12), ten vendor renders from the telco.com media library, and the legacy NetZoom stencil "Telco Systems" (2022), master T-Metro 8001 (F). NO VENDOR IMAGE IS SQUARE-ON - every render is a three-quarter view - and no installation guide is public. One file in the library, telco.com 2021/03/8001.png, is not this product: it is a T-Metro 8104 render filed under the 8001's name.

stencil-is-another-build.note: The 2022 NetZoom master T-Metro 8001 (F) is NOT this face and is not used for geometry: it puts the logo and lamps at the right, has no fan-tray wheel, and draws the five port blocks 2 mm apart where the render has 5-6 mm. Its one agreement with the render is the colour-coded lamp strip under the middle of the port row (stencil 5 x 26.06 mm, render 5 x 25.4-26.4), which is what confirms the strip is real rather than a render artefact. It is most likely the 2019 build's face; the current one is drawn.
